editorial:
Imagine the pressure of being the fastest person in the country while the whole world is watching and judging who you are. That is exactly where you find Nikki Hiltz in this powerful documentary. You get a front-row seat to Nikki's life as a trans nonbinary athlete fighting for a spot in the Olympics. It is not just about the running, though. You also get to see the sweet and honest relationship between Nikki and their partner, Emma. The vibe is very intimate, making you feel like you are part of their inner circle during one of the most stressful years of their life.

What really works here is how the movie balances the high energy of the races with the quiet, emotional moments at home. The pacing keeps you on edge, and the footage of the competitions is stunning. If you can, watch this streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to really see the intensity on the track, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection if you love sports docs. It is a great pick for anyone who likes stories about overcoming odds. Just be ready for some heavy emotional moments alongside the victory laps.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up at the Olympic trials where the tension reaches its peak. You see Nikki push through the pain and the noise of the crowd to secure their spot on the team. Instead of focusing only on the medal, the final scenes show Nikki and Emma celebrating their growth as a couple. It ends with a quiet moment of reflection, showing that Nikki found peace with their identity regardless of the public's opinion.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves underdog stories and true human drama.
